name: Ransomware Hits Records and Jail Systems
description: Ransomware encrypts records management and jail management systems; deputies fall back to paper booking while systems are rebuilt from backups.
assumptions: Public-safety response continues; the loss is administrative rebuild and overtime.
County policy prohibits ransom payment; recovery is from backups.
Secondary loss covers case-processing delays and legal exposure from missed deadlines.

name: Dispatch System Disruption
description: An attack on computer-aided dispatch forces radio-and-paper dispatching, slowing response coordination until the system is restored.
assumptions: Manual dispatch procedures are drilled quarterly and sustain operations at reduced tempo.
Primary loss covers restoration, overtime, and mutual-aid costs.
Secondary loss covers liability exposure if response delays are alleged in litigation.

name: Evidence System Tampering
description: Unauthorized access to the digital evidence management system raises chain-of-custody challenges across active prosecutions.
asset: Digital evidence management and chain of custody
threat: Insider or intruder altering evidence records
assumptions: A single confirmed tampering event taints every case touching the affected storage.
Primary loss covers forensic audit and re-validation of evidence handling.
Secondary loss covers dismissed cases, civil liability, and public-trust damage.

name: Criminal Justice Records Exposure
description: An intrusion exposes CJIS-protected records including victim, witness, and informant details held in investigative files.
asset: Criminal justice information and investigative files
assumptions: Exposure of informant or witness data drives the high-end estimates.
Primary loss covers investigation, notification, and CJIS-mandated remediation.
Secondary loss covers protective measures for exposed persons and civil claims.

name: Procurement Payment Fraud
description: Fraudsters impersonate equipment and construction vendors to redirect county public-safety procurement payments.
assumptions: Public bid records make vendor relationships and payment timing visible to fraudsters.
Primary loss is unrecovered funds after bank and insurance recovery.
Secondary loss covers audit findings and state oversight remediation.
